title: Adverbs of Time
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the adverbs and example sentences were reconstructed from context and standard German.
objectives: I can say on which day and at what time of day something happens
I can talk about the past, the present and the future with time adverbs
I can put actions in order with zuerst, dann and danach
I can say how often I do something

expressions.de: Am Montag beginnt der Unterricht um 15 Uhr.
expressions.en: On Monday the class begins at 3 pm.

expressions.de: Ab und zu brauche ich eine Pause.
expressions.en: Now and then I need a break.

patterns.en: I waited a long time for it.
Today I want to drink tea.

grammar.title: Three questions: wann, wie lange, wie oft
grammar.body: Adverbs of time answer three questions: **wann?** (when), **wie lange?** (how long) and **wie oft?** (how often). They do not change their form. When an adverb of time stands in first position, the verb comes second (V2): **Heute** *kommt* mein Mann.

examples.en: She is on the phone right now.

grammar.title: Days and parts of the day
grammar.body: Add **-s** to a day or part of the day to say that something happens regularly: **montags** = every Monday. You can also say **am Montag** for one particular Monday. For times of the day use **morgens, vormittags, mittags, nachmittags, abends, nachts**.
grammar.ar: الإضافة -s تعني التكرار: montags = كل يوم اثنين.

examples.en: In the evening we all go for a walk.
She has to travel in the morning.

grammar.title: Past, present, future
grammar.body: **Past:** vorgestern, gestern, früher, damals. **Present:** heute, jetzt, nun, gerade, sofort, heutzutage. **Future:** morgen, übermorgen, bald, später. Do not mix up **morgen** (tomorrow) and **morgens** (in the morning).

examples.de: Früher habe ich kein Gemüse gegessen.
examples.en: In the past I did not eat vegetables.

examples.de: Damals war ich ein kleiner Junge.
examples.en: Back then I was a little boy.
She is going to have a baby soon.

grammar.title: Sequence: zuerst, dann, danach, später
grammar.body: Use these adverbs to put actions in order. Remember V2: the verb stays in second position after them.

examples.de: Zuerst sollst du lesen und dann übersetzen.
examples.en: First you should read and then translate.

examples.de: Danach gehen wir einkaufen und später essen wir Eis.
examples.en: After that we go shopping and later we eat ice cream.

grammar.title: How often? From always to never
grammar.body: From 100 % to 0 %: **immer, fast immer, meistens, oft / häufig, manchmal / ab und zu, selten, fast nie, nie**.

examples.de: Um diese Zeit bin ich meistens schon im Bett.
examples.en: At this time I am mostly already in bed.

examples.de: Sie kommt sehr selten aus dem Haus.
examples.en: She very rarely leaves the house.

mistakes.why: After an adverb in first position the verb comes second.

mistakes.wrong: Ich habe ihn nicht nie gesehen.
mistakes.why: *nie* already means never; do not add *nicht*.

pronunciation.tip: Round your lips as for 'oo' and say 'ee'. *übermorgen, früher, später* (ä sounds like 'e').

lines.de: Samstags schlafe ich lange, und abends gehe ich oft spazieren.
lines.en: On Saturdays I sleep late, and in the evening I often go for a walk.

tip: Learn the adverbs in groups (past, present, future, frequency) and make one true sentence about your own life for each group.

comprehension.q: What do you add to a day to say that something happens every week on that day?
Which three questions do adverbs of time answer?
What is the difference between morgen and morgens?
comprehension.a: morgen means tomorrow; morgens means in the morning.

comprehension.q: How do you say 'never' and 'almost never'?

exercises.title: Match the adverbs
exercises.instructions: Match each German adverb with its English meaning.

exercises.title: Choose the right adverb
exercises.instructions: Choose the adverb that fits the sentence.

items.q: ___ war ich ein kleiner Junge. (Damals / Morgen)
items.expl: The sentence is about the past.
The present tense *bekommt* with a future meaning needs *bald*.

items.q: Er kommt ___ zu spät. Das ist immer so. (immer / nie)
items.expl: *Das ist immer so* = it is always like that.

items.q: Ich habe ihn ___ gesehen. Wir kennen uns nicht. (nie / oft)
items.expl: We do not know each other, so never.

items.q: Ich muss ___ gehen. Der Bus kommt gleich. (jetzt / vorgestern)
Zuerst lesen wir, ___ übersetzen wir. (dann / gestern)

exercises.title: Days of the week
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence with the correct German form.

items.q: Der Unterricht beginnt am ___ um 15 Uhr. (Monday)
___ gehen wir alle spazieren. (In the evening)

exercises.title: Put the words in order
exercises.instructions: Write the correct sentence. Begin with a capital letter.

items.a: Sie telefoniert gerade. / Gerade telefoniert sie.
Ich habe manchmal Kopfschmerzen. / Manchmal habe ich Kopfschmerzen.
Wir gehen abends spazieren. / Abends gehen wir spazieren.

summary: Adverbs of time answer wann, wie lange and wie oft and never change form.
Add -s to a day or part of the day for regular actions: montags, abends.
Past: gestern, früher, damals. Present: heute, jetzt, gerade. Future: morgen, bald, später.
Frequency: immer, meistens, oft, manchmal, selten, nie.
